instructions: Rinse 1 1/2 cups basmati rice until the water runs mostly clear. Add it to a medium pot with 2 1/4 cups water and 1/2 tsp of the salt, bring to a boil over high heat, then cover, turn the heat to low and cook for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.
Meanwhile, coarsely crush the peppercorns with a mortar and pestle, or under a heavy pan on a cutting board. Whisk the yogurt until smooth. Cut the paneer into 3/4-inch cubes.
Roughly chop the onion, ginger, garlic and green chili. Heat 1 tbsp of the ghee in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the cinnamon, cardamom and cloves and cook for 20 seconds, until fragrant.
Add the onion, ginger, garlic, chili and cashews and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until golden. Let it cool for 5 minutes, then take out the cinnamon, cardamom and cloves.
Transfer the rest to a blender with 1/3 cup water and blend until smooth.

Heat the remaining 2 tbsp ghee in the same skillet over medium-low heat. Add the bay leaf and caraway seeds for 20 seconds, then add the onion paste. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring, until oil separates around the edges.
Stir in 3/4 tsp of the crushed pepper for 1 minute. Add the chili powder, garam masala and coriander and cook for 1 minute.
Turn off the heat and stir in the yogurt, then 3/4 cup water and 3/4 tsp salt. Return to low heat and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until little specks of oil show on top.
Add the paneer, turn off the heat and stir in the cream. Take out the bay leaf.
Top with chopped cilantro and the last 1/4 tsp crushed pepper. Serve with the rice.
method_notes: Cup of Yum leads (4.5 from 20 ratings): a cashew and onion paste simmered in ghee, yogurt added off the heat, crushed black pepper for the flavor and paneer stirred in at the end. Cook with Manali (4.91 from 10) and My Ginger Garlic Kitchen (5.0 from 6) agree on the paste and add milk or a paneer marinade, which were left out. Kewra water and mace were skipped, and the pepper is kept to a gentle amount.
